verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The chain is stated in Lean in exactly the same three steps, with two routine rewritings. (i) The integrand: Lean writes the endpoint as -(1/2) ∫_{(X,∞)} E(x,η)²/x dx where the paper writes -∫_X^∞ E(x,η)²/(2x) dx; these agree pointwise and `halfKernel_eq` (NominalProfile.lean:1679) is the Lean lemma that moves the 1/2 across the integral sign. (ii) The middle equality Π_0(η) + C_p(X,η) = C_p(X,η) - C_p(∞,η) is `canonical_past_identity` with k = halfKernel E η: it says -(∫_{(0,∞)} k) + ∫_{(0,X]} k = -(∫_{(X,∞)} k), i.e. the paper's identity after substituting C_p(∞,η) = -Π_0(η), which `outgoing_axis_halfKernel` supplies. (iii) Lean's integral over Ioc 0 X versus the paper's cumulative increment C_p(X,η) = primitive (f²) differ only by the endpoint of a null set. The Lean versions carry integrability (`IntegrableOn k (Ioi 0)`) and parameter hypotheses (hη, SmallDebt, separation) that the paper leaves implicit in its standing assumptions.
